entry.dc:title: Curved conveyor system connecting an open pit mine with a power station
entry.dc:creator: Bruewer T.
entry.dc:description: In western Turkey a downhill long distance conveyor system with horizontal and vertical curves was designed and built by Krupp Industrietechnik and the Turkish company Gama Endustri Tesisleri. The exact planning of the route of this conveyor system was only possible with the aid of a CAD system and a simulation program for conveyors. The latest drive technology and controlled brake and pretensioning systems enable uncritical system behavior to be achieved in all load and operating conditions. The first year of operation confirmed the expectations the customer had of the system.

entry.dc:title: Truck dispatching in an open pit mine
entry.dc:creator: Soumis F.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: In an open pit mine operated by trucks and shovels, the trucks should be dispatched from the crusher to the shovels in such a way that the productivity of trucks and shovels in maximized while maintaining a rational production plan as well as obtaining target grades and other objectives with small variations at the entrance to the concentrator. To solve the dispatching problem we present a three step approach. First we select shovel locations with a man-machine interactive system. This step combines operator expertise and linear programming optimisation. In the second step, we establish an optimal strategy (production plan) for a certain period of time by solving a network problem with non-linear costs associated with estimates of trucks’ and shovels’ waiting times and the quality objectives. The solution gives, for each shovel, the best access paths, the trucks’ and shovels’ estimated waiting times and an estimate of the number of trucks loaded per unit of time. In the last step we dispatch each truck in real-time by solving an assigment problem, taking into account the next 15 trucks, which are becoming available for dispatching in order to get a series of dispatches which will realize the optimal strategy. © 1989, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Fragmentation systems design in surface mines: An expert system application
entry.dc:creator: Paul J.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Mining Engineers in charge of open pit mine planning very often face decision making situations dealing with the selection of the most economical method for the removal of overburden. Ripping versus conventional drilling and blasting are the options considered. The choice of a particular overburden removal method depends upon the physicomechanical properties of the overburden material as well as the various cost factors involved in the process. The analysis of technoeconomical factors, related to different methods of overburden removal in surface mines, needs detailed study and investigation by a technical expert. The expert system “FRAGMENTATION” has been developed to help and expedite the decision making process involving the selection of overburden removal method in surface mines. Furthermore, this expert system can be used for detailed design of overburden removal in open pit mines, specifically for determining charge geometry placement and cost analysis. © 1989, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: The influence of mining adjacent deposits on rock pressure dynamics in the Khibini Massif
entry.dc:creator: Kozyrev A.
entry.dc:description: A finite element method is used to study the problem of the stressed state of a rock mass when deposits are developed, in two underground mines and an open pit mine. The stress state of the initial rock mass and at the following stages of mining are discussed. When large volumes of rock mass are mined out under high tectonic stresses, the reciprocal influence of mining of adjacent deposits on the stress state of the rock mass is shown to be substantial. As a result, technogenous earthquakes, rock bursts and rock mass movements along natural jointing planes take place. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: An application of discrete mathematics in the design of an open pit mine
entry.dc:creator: Caccetta L.
entry.dc:description: The determination of the "optimum pit limit" of a mine is considered to be a fundamental problem in mine planning as it provides information which is essential in the evaluation of the economic potential of a mineral deposit, and in the formulation of long-, intermediate-, and short-range mine plans. A number of mathematical techniques have been proposed to solve this problem, some of the more elaborate ones posing considerable computational problems. In this paper we discuss the development and implementation of a graph-theoretic technique originally proposed by Lerchs and Grossman. Our implementation strategy involves the use of a dynamic programming technique to "bound" the optimum. © 1988.

entry.dc:title: WORLD'S LARGEST HYDRAULIC SHOVEL, O&K'S RH 300, NOW OPERATING AT CHUQUICAMATA, WORLD'S LARGEST COPPER MINE.
entry.dc:creator: O'Neil T.
entry.dc:description: The O&K RH 300 hydraulic excavator has been put into service to move overburden and mine ore at the Chuquicamata open pit mine of the Chilean state copper mining company, Corporacion Nacional de Cobre de Chile (Codelco). The hydraulic excavator is the second of these units to be put into use. The other unit operates at Northern Strip Mining's open pit coal operation in England.

entry.dc:title: Role of geotechnical engineering in the development and operation of Syncrude's open pit mine and tailings pond
entry.dc:creator: Fair A.
entry.dc:description: The Syncrude Canada Ltd. open pit mine and tailings pond, located near Fort McMurray in northern Alberta, represent two of the largest operations of their kind anywhere in the world. This paper is intended to provide an overview of the geotechnical role in the development and operation of the Syncrude project. The paper chronicles the geotechnical input into the project, beginning with the large scale test pits which were utilized to provide a basis for mine equipment selection and to evaluate highwall performance. Sophisticated instrumentation monitoring programs were developed to ensure the ongoing safety of major equipment operating along the highwall crest. The location and orientation of the pit have had a major impact on highwall performance. Considerable effort has also been devoted to understanding the unique material properties of the oil sand. Design of the tailings dyke has been based on the observational approach. Consequently, geotechnical parameters and monitoring programs continue to regulate the design and ensure the successful completion of the dykes. More recently, risk assessment studies, based on geotechnical considerations, are being utilized to help assess optimum operating strategies for both the tailings pond and highwall slopes. A comparison of the original geotechnical concerns with present day performance is also presented in the paper.

entry.dc:title: Case examples and developments in open pit mine stability
entry.dc:creator: Brawner C.
entry.dc:description: The reduced demand for coals and many minerals has led to substantial advances in geomechanics which are aimed at ensuring efficiency and reduce mining costs. These advances can provide major economic and safety benefits in various areas of surface mining in the near future. Stability on surface mining projects is primarily dependent on five factors. These include structural geology, groundwater, blasting and the existence of weak layers, particularly clayey gouge or clay infill. Case examples of stability on many surface mines including coal mines are presented in this paper.

entry.dc:title: COAL OF THE CHERNIGOVSKII OPEN PIT MINE - AN ADDITIONAL RESOURCE OF COAL FOR COKING.
entry.dc:creator: Zolotukhin Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Coke and Chemistry U S S R
entry.dc:description: Screenings of coal from the Chernigovskii Open Pit Mine may be used in coking charges if coal from section no. 1, produced in a zone of partial oxidation, is excluded in the processing of the washery of the integrated plant. In order to improve the properties of the charge, particularly to increase its shrinkage properties, it is desirable to fully replace the type OS coal of the Sibirginskii Open Pit Mine with screenings of coal of the Chernigovskii Open Pit Mine in the quantity of 10% of the run-of-mine charge. The effect of the screenings on all the operating indices of the coking plant should be determined in greater detail. Coal of the Chernigovskii Open Pit Mine may be considered a good feedstock for production of low-phosphorus coke.

entry.dc:title: Testing the Possibility of Combusting Open Pit Mine Moscanica Coal - Zenica.
entry.dc:creator: Vuletic V.
entry.dc:description: The paper presents the results of full-scale testing of coal from openpit mine Moscanica, belonging to the brown coal mines Zenica in order to define the possibility of its industrial use, within the framework or activities related to opening and start-up of the openpit Moscanica deposit. Testing was carried out in the fireplace of a section boiler with a flat crawling grain in power generating plant at Zenica.

entry.dc:title: U. S. BORAX.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Boron-containing compounds are used in the manufacture of heat-resistant glass, fibreglass, porcelain, enamel, ceramics, soaps and detergents, fire retardents and other products. Worldwide demand for borates is about 975,000 t/y B//2O//3, of which the U. S. A. supplies about 60%. Over half this is produced by the United States Borax & Chemical Corporation, a wholly-owned subsidiary of RTZ. U. S. Borax operates an open pit mine at Boron in the Mojave Desert.

entry.dc:title: Indicator kriging for unit vectors: Rock joint orientations
entry.dc:creator: Young D.S.
entry.dc:description: Indicator kriging (IK) is extended to analyze three-dimensional random unit vectors and evaluate the local probability distribution of rock joint orientations in geological formations. The pole vector representing joint orientations is regionalized and projected on a plane normal to the mean attitude of the joint family and centered at the mean. A two-dimensional cutoff system is developed to define the indicator variable, and corresponding indicator variograms and indicator kriging. The cutoff system defines probability regions similar to those of a bivariate distribution, concentric rings sliced into radial sectors. A case study made on an open pit mine proved positively the efficiency of IK and encourages its applications to localized probabilistic structural modeling for geotechnical or geohydrological analysis and oil and gas reservoir analysis. © 1987 International Association for Mathematical Geology.

entry.dc:title: OPTIMIZATION OF OPEN PIT SHORT- AND LONG-RANGE PRODUCTION SCHEDULING.
entry.dc:creator: Fytas K.
entry.dc:description: A computer model has been developed which is capable of evaluating alternative production schedules (long- and short-range) of an open pit mine once the ultimate pit limits have been defined. The model user can choose the best alternative according to cash flow considerations and the particular mining conditions. The model involves a combination of simulation for long-range production scheduling and linear programming for short-range scheduling.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW AUSTRALIAN GOLD MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Late last year gold production began at Mount Leyshon open pit mine in Northern Queensland following the commissioning of heap leaching facilities on site. Once full scale operation is reached, the mine is expected to move some 1Mt/y mineralized material, producing 46,000 oz/y gold in its first three years of production. Mt. Leyshon represents an investment of A13. 5 million (A equals POUND 2. 3) for its owners, Pan Australian Mining Ltd, a young and developing Australian mining company. Current ore reserves are reported to be 6. 3 Mt grading 1. 8g/t gold and 4. 8g/t silver, and Pan Aust are confident that these will increase substantilly, with additions to both the oxide and primary ore reserve, 'significantly extending the mine life'.

entry.dc:title: Comparing Calculations with Measurement Results for Pulverized Lignite Flame.
entry.dc:creator: Modlinski Z.
entry.dc:description: Calculation results obtained with the aid of an electronic data processing facility regarding the combustion of pulverized lignite from the Brieske open pit mine (East Germany) in the swirling flame of an experimental burner are presented. The test results presented in earlier papers have been utilized in the flame model. Kinetic constants are derived. The calculation results obtained are compared with experimental results obtained from the flame. The results coincide qualitatively.

entry.dc:title: The use of dynamic programming for open pit mine design: Some practical implications
entry.dc:creator: Wright E.
entry.dc:description: Determining the optimum ultimate-pit limits can be justified when analysing low-grade and/or inhomogeneous surfacial deposits. Such deposits require investigations of a range of ultimate pits for correct economic judgement. A prerequisite for such economic analyses is a fast and accurate method for determining the multiple pit shells to be analysed. Dynamic Programming (DP) offers an advantageous alternative to both the Lerchs-Grossman algorithm and the moving-cone method, for the design of the multiple pits required for such economic sensitivity analyses. This paper examines some of the practical aspects involved in using dynamic programming for ultimate pit design (UPD). The basics are discussed and some DP proposals are reviewed. The question of the optimum ultimate pit versus the practical need for generating acceptable non-optimum pits, using minimum computing times and core storage, is examined. Results from tests with various refinements of the 3-dimensional dynamic programming approach for ultimate pit design proposed by Wilke and Wright are discussed. The indication is that ultimate-pit results, which, in terms of total economic values, are no worse than those designed by the moving-cone method, can be obtained with the modified approaches using only fractions of the computing times required by the moving-cone method. © 1987 Elsevier Science Publishers B.V.

entry.dc:title: Settlement observations of open pit mine backfill
entry.dc:creator: Thomson S.
entry.dc:description: Reclaimed land from open pit mining operations must have essentially completed settling under self-weight and must be capable of supporting light structures before it can be returned to the public domain. The settlement of the spoil from one open pit mining operation west of Edmonton, Alberta, was monitored by a series of magnet extensometers installed in boreholes. Time-settlement plots indicated that self-weight settlement occurs within a 3 to 5 year period. Tests of individual small footings pointed out the necessity to place shallow foundations on beneficiated soil. The results of a second series of small footings led to the founding of an 8 m×10 m prototype instrumented, reinforced foundation on a 1 m thick soil/flyash mat. Observations to date indicated an entirely acceptable settlement pattern.

entry.dc:title: Microseismic data processing associated with monitoring of mine slope instabilities
entry.dc:creator: Stuart N.
entry.dc:description: Microseismic monitoring in open pit operations has been carried out at the Cardinal River Mine near Hinton, Alberta. The target region was an extremely extensive slope in highly tectonised, jurassic, coal bearing strata. The project was experimental in nature. The aim of this data flow analysis is to examine the possibility of using certain parameters as a prediction of failure, to examine where improvements seem possible in the system and how the results might be used in conjunction with other types of monitoring that are currently, or might potentially be used at Cardinal River or other open pit mine operations.

entry.dc:title: STUDY OF THE POSSIBILITY OF REPLACING COKE WITH LEAN COAL IN AGGLOMERATION OF PHOSPHORITES.
entry.dc:creator: Puzankov V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
entry.dc:description: The authors give the results of investigations to more correctly determine the agglomeration parameters of phosphorites, the indices of the process, and the quality of the product, when using coal from the Krasnogorsk Open Pit mine from the zone of thermal contact metamorphism, characterized by complete absence of tars. The results of the investigations provided support for the previously demonstrated possibility of full equivalent (by carbon) substitution of metallurgical coal in agglomeration of phosphorites with Krasnogorsk coal. It was shown that the parameters and indices of the process, as well as the product quality, are similar when this substitution is made.

entry.dc:title: STUDY OF THE BEHAVIOR OF NERYUNGRA COAL IN COKING CHARGES.
entry.dc:creator: Shreider E.M.
entry.prism:publicationName: Coke Chemistry USSR English Translation of Koks I Khimiya
entry.dc:description: It is shown that use of 10% coal from the Neryungra Open Pit Mine in place of (type OS, SS, K) Kuznetsk coal decreased the yield of cleaned charge (by 1. 5%) with a simultaneous increase in its ash (by an average of 0. 64%). There was an increase in the losses of coal with the tailings and middlings. It is technologically infeasible to clean Neryungra coal together with coal from the Pechora and Kuznetsk Coalfields. The ash of the coke from the charge containing Neryungra coal rose by an average of 0. 7%. However, the total strength of the coke increased slightly. With the commissioning of a washery at the open pit mine using dense media (expected ash of the concentrate less than 9. 5%) it will be feasible to conduct additional studies on the possibility of use of the concentrate as an admixture to coal charges.

entry.dc:title: REVIEW AND SUGGESTION FOR SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH WORK ON MINE AUTOMATION IN CIMR.
entry.dc:creator: Zhang Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Changsha Kuangshan Yanjiuyuan Jikan Quarterly of the Changsha Institute of Mining Research
entry.dc:description: The author summarizes the major achievements on mine automation research work of CIMR in the past 30 years. Suggestions on the direction of research work and measures that should be required for developing underground and open pit mine automation of China in the future.

entry.dc:title: EMPIRICAL VALUATION OF A PROCESS TO HOMOGENIZE BROWN COAL PROPERTIES AT STORAGE YARDS OF THE BELCHATOW OPEN PIT MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Lazowski A.
entry.dc:description: The method of investigating the process of homogenizing brown coal properties at storage yards of the Belchatow open pit mine is described and the results discussed in detail. The estimated values of the degrees of inhomogeneity and homogeneity of the brown coal are given, the latter being the quality coefficient of the investigated process.

entry.dc:title: INCO'S NEW OPEN PIT DELIVERS LOW-COST NICKEL ORE.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Filling the processing pipeline with lowcost mined nickel ore was Inco's main motive for developing its new Thompson open pit mine in northern Manitoba, Canada. The new pit, which mines the crown pillar of the Thompson underground mine, replaces ore that was previously railed from the Pipe open-pit, located 20 min to the south. The decision to bring the Thompson open-pit mine into production rather than rejuvenate or develop any of the other underground mines was based primarily of the fact that surface mining technology, personnel, and equipment already existed at the Pipe open pit. Mining is carried out in the pit two shifts/day operating on 45-ft benches with 25-ft berms. The ultimate dimensions of the mine will be 5,100 ft along the north-south direction, 800 ft in the east-west direction, and 400 ft below surface at its deepest point.

entry.dc:title: RECENT DEVELOPMENTS IN OPEN PIT MINE DESIGN AND PLANNING.
entry.dc:creator: Bose A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of the Institution of Engineers India Mining Engineering Division
entry.dc:description: Ultimate open pit mine designs originally required many months of effort. With the advent of computers, such manual efforts have greatly reduced. In all advanced countries, surface mine design is invariably computer assisted. The paper discusses a few concepts and techniques being adopted for open pit mine design.

entry.dc:title: Preliminary design of a deep open pit mine ( Bukit Asam): an exercise in the engineering method.
entry.dc:creator: Shields D.
entry.prism:publicationName: Geotechnical Stability in Surface Mining Proc Symposium Calgary 1986
entry.dc:description: Initial planning for the development of an open pit coal mine in Sumatra, Indonesia, required detailed appraisal of the difficult geotechnical conditions at the site. One preliminary mine plan called for a pit 180 m deep; all plans involved pits at least 140 m deep. It was important that the pit slopes be as steep as possible to minimize costs; on the other hand, care had to be taken to ensure the slopes would not be so steep that they would be unsafe. -from Author
